learning_objective: 🎯 Empower yourself by learning your rights as a buyer, how to identify fake products, and the legal steps to take if you are cheated in the market!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: A consumer is anyone who buys goods or hires services for personal use (not for resale) by paying a price.
Consumers often face issues like adulterated food, defective electronics, false weights and measures, misleading advertisements, and poor after-sales service.
The CPA is a vital Indian law designed to protect consumers. It provides a three-tier system (District, State, and National levels) for consumers to file complaints easily and cheaply.
As a consumer, you have the Right to: Safety, Be Informed, Choose, Be Heard, Seek Redressal, and Consumer Education.
These are logos given by the government guaranteeing product quality. Examples include ISI (industrial products), Agmark (agricultural products), and FPO (fruit products).

fun_activity.title: 🔍 The Quality Mark Hunt
fun_activity.instructions: Go on a scavenger hunt in your kitchen and bathroom! Try to find products that have the 'ISI' mark (check appliances like irons or geysers), 'Agmark' (check spices or oil), and the green/red vegetarian/non-vegetarian dots.

exam_tips: 📌 Memorize all 6 Consumer Rights under the Consumer Protection Act.
📌 Know the difference between a Guarantee (promise to replace the item) and a Warranty (promise to repair the item).
📌 Be able to match the standard mark to its product category (e.g., Agmark for agriculture, ISI for electronics/cement).
quick_recap: ⭐ 'Caveat Emptor' means 'Let the buyer beware'—consumers must be alert and educated.
⭐ Always ask for a bill or cash memo; it is your legal proof of purchase if you need to file a complaint.
⭐ The Right to Redressal means you have the right to a fair settlement of your genuine grievances.
